channel.title: The Voynich Times
channel.description: The Voynich Times covers the Voynich manuscript, uncracked ciphers, real treasure hunts like The Secret, and the mystery-puzzle hobby — news, features, and a daily cabinet of curiosities.

item.title: The Voynich Times Collector is open to everyone — catalogue your mystery-game collection against the full Times database!
item.description: The Collector leaves beta behind: sign in with Google to browse 2,770 catalogued mystery games, puzzle boxes, escape-room games, and treasure hunts; mark what you own, want, have played, or have solved; keep ratings and notes; and sync your shelves to your own Google Sheet. Links to published reviews and a shelf of free public-domain puzzle books are built in.

item.title: New! Cryptogram Puzzle Post ships The Stormlamp Rituals Issue 06 — Jack Fallows' puzzle zine is back from the printers and on sale now!
item.description: Jack Fallows announced on November 7 that The Stormlamp Rituals Issue 06, the latest Cryptogram Puzzle Post zine, is back from the printers and shipping worldwide this week. The 36-page full-colour zine follows the young witch Anna through hand-illustrated prose and puzzles, with loose pages and a prize postcard in an envelope inside the back cover and an online hint system offering three clues for every puzzle. It is a very limited print run of a Patreon-exclusive zine, now on sale to everyone for £12.00 through the Cryptogram Puzzle Post Big Cartel store.

item.title: PRE-ORDER ALERT! Gareth Moore's Catch the Imposter crashes a manor dinner party — 26 guests, one fraud, and a puzzle trail to unmask them!
item.description: Gareth Moore and Laura Jayne Ayres drop you into a manor dinner party where sudoku, mazes and logic puzzles unmask one imposter among 26 guests.

item.title: New! Red Herring Games rides west — Wanted!, a Wild West escape room in a box, is coming soon to Kickstarter
item.description: Red Herring Games announced Wanted! on November 5: a Wild West escape room in a box, and the newest edition of the company's long-running puzzle box line. Players step into the Wild West and use the information in the box to track down the town's most wanted outlaw. The Kickstarter pre-launch page is live now, with the campaign expected to launch in the next couple of weeks.

item.title: Deadbolt Mystery Society opens Nigma November — a month of puzzles and giveaways kicks off with a dungeon challenge!
item.description: Deadbolt Mystery Society announced Nigma November on November 4: a month-long run of puzzles and giveaways through November. The challenges run on the company's social channels — the first is live now on its Facebook and Instagram and is dungeon-themed, with more to follow through the month. Follow along at facebook.com/deadboltmysterysociety and instagram.com/deadboltmysterysociety.

item.title: New! Scarlet Envelope's Santa's Code Machine lands on its website — crack Santa's Code, then encrypt a secret message of your own!
item.description: Scarlet Envelope's folded Christmas puzzle card Santa's Code Machine is now available on the company's website, announced November 3 in its Newsletter X. Players sneak into Santa's toy factory while he snoozes and solve six puzzles (difficulty 3/5, about 40 minutes) to decrypt Santa's Code — then use that code to encrypt their own secret message before gifting the card, which comes with a red envelope and a cheat card. It is CA$14.00, marked down from CA$15.00, and the company says last year's inventory is very limited.

item.title: PRE-ORDER ALERT! Odd Pieces skips Kickstarter for the first time — new 500-piece Perspective Puzzles launch as a direct presale, and the picture changes as you build!
item.description: Odd Pieces, the studio behind the Mystery Puzzles series, announced its first-ever launch off Kickstarter on November 2: Perspective Puzzles, a brand-new 500-piece line sold as a direct presale at oddpieces.com. Each puzzle in the Inner Child series (Siblings, My Cats and Me, Playroom) starts from the box art, then the image changes partway through the build — one big shift that changes the meaning of the whole picture. The puzzles are already printed and ship mid-November 2026, with early-bird pricing at $28 for one (list $42) or $58 for the set of three.

item.title: Times Now finds the cure for doomscrolling hiding in a puzzle book — Murdle and Can You Solve the Murder? turn readers into the detectives!
item.description: Times Now explores the puzzle-book revival, spotlighting G.T. Karber's Murdle and Antony Johnston's Can You Solve the Murder? as interactive mysteries readers solve themselves.

item.title: KICKSTARTER ALERT! The Medusa Experience leaves 34 dead in a French manor — solve it in five weeks, then watch the answer as a feature film!
item.description: De Vérité et de Spectacle's Medusa Experience is an ARG murder mystery built around a manor party where 34 people died with no wounds, no forced entry and no cause of death. Backers receive a film-canister evidence box, then investigate for five weeks as new evidence drops for everyone at once, and submit a single theory — the solution is revealed in a feature film on Halloween 2027. A Kickstarter "Project We Love," it launched October 28 and was funded within a day ($4,311 of a $2,234 goal at filing); the campaign ends November 25, with boxes shipping autumn 2027.

item.title: KICKSTARTER ALERT! PostCurious's Witching Hour closes at $251,359 — 3,266 backers solve the cursed maze, more than sixteen times its $15,000 goal!
item.description: PostCurious's The Witching Hour, a narrative puzzle adventure by Rita Orlov, has closed successfully on Kickstarter with $251,359 pledged from 3,266 backers against a $15,000 goal. Players solve their way through a cursed maze to untangle a mystery of the past. Estimated delivery is August 2027.

item.title: Starts at 60 sharpens the pencils — The Killer Isn't Alice, A Puzzling Pursuit and a missing-husband case top its brain-busting puzzle-book lineup!
item.description: Starts at 60 reviews a stack of puzzle books, from Iris Starling's 46,600-suspect murder case to Lorena Carrington's Outback newspaper-killer road trip.

item.title: Salt Entertainment cracks open the Lament Configuration — an escape-room-style Hellraiser game leads a new tabletop line for the horror classic's 40th!
item.description: Salt Entertainment's licensed Hellraiser line includes an escape-room-style tabletop game inspired by the Lament Configuration puzzle box, alongside dice and social deduction games.

item.title: Firefinch sharpens its knives — Orlando Murrin's Curdle summons six celebrity chefs to a critic's estate, and readers must unmask his killer!
item.description: Orlando Murrin's interactive whodunnit Curdle from Firefinch has readers solve maps, plans and puzzles to unmask who murdered a restaurant critic hosting six celebrity chefs.
The Bookseller reports booming puzzle-book sales, with Murdle and The Killer Isn't Alice inspiring a wave of immersive murder-mystery puzzle books.

item.title: NEW! Key Enigma reveals DUEL — the first Escape Duel, a two-team divider game racing to disable a dangerous device, coming soon to Kickstarter!
item.description: Key Enigma used its Red Kraken shipping update and SPIEL Essen preview page to reveal DUEL, billed as the first Escape Duel. Two teams separated by a huge interactive divider must share information they cannot show each other, manipulate the divider, and combine clues to disable a device in time. The Kickstarter campaign is still a few months away, with a very limited production run, tokens, dice and cards, and a Kickstarter offer that includes a DUEL expansion; no price or launch date was given.

item.title: Publishers Weekly cracks a seven-figure case — Tytora signs seven more Murdle books, sending Deductive Logico into new puzzle types and even romantasy!
item.description: St. Martin's new Tytora puzzle imprint signed G.T. Karber to a seven-book Murdle deal, expanding the murder-mystery logic puzzles into new formats and genres.

item.title: Hunt A Killer stakes out London Comic Con — Relatable's mystery range opens a UK case file in its games-lounge debut!
item.description: Character Options showcased the new UK Hunt-A-Killer range in Relatable's London Comic Con games lounge, with an influencer campaign stalking Halloween and the festive season.

item.title: BuzzFeed puts Murdoku first in the lineup — 80 crime scenes lead its "Who would buy this? Oh right, me" treat list!
item.description: BuzzFeed's treat-yourself roundup opens with Manuel Garand's Murdoku, a visual Murdle-inspired logic book of 80 crime scenes from bakeries to the opera.

item.title: BuzzFeed's thirty-somethings never outgrew their Sherlock phase — Murdle Volume 1 and Merry Murdle land in the cart!
item.description: BuzzFeed's buy-what-you-want roundup slips in G.T. Karber's Murdle Volume 1 deduction puzzle book, with the festive Merry Murdle as a seasonal pick.

item.title: KICKSTARTER ALERT! TED-Ed pries Pandora's box open again — a Pandora's Legacy sequel is plotting its spring 2027 Kickstarter return!
item.description: TED-Ed is preparing a sequel to its Pandora's Legacy puzzle adventure game and is surveying backers to help shape the coming campaign.

item.title: BuzzFeed corks a riddle under lock and key — Uncommon Goods' Unlock The Wine escape room game joins its gift-giver hall of fame!
item.description: BuzzFeed's Uncommon Goods gift roundup features Unlock The Wine, an escape room card game of 160-plus riddles guarding a locked bottle.

item.title: ColombiaOne rebinds the Voynich riddle — Davis & Layfield's peer-reviewed singulion study says our favorite manuscript began as loose folded sheets!
item.description: Lisa Fagin Davis and Colin Layfield's Digital Medievalist study argues the Voynich Manuscript began as loose folded sheets later bound out of order.

item.title: Space Cowboys picks the US lock on Unlock! New Game Adventures — Heat, Carcassonne & 7 Wonders turn into escape rooms on shelves today!
item.description: Space Cowboys' fifteenth Unlock! box brings three app-guided card escape adventures set in the worlds of Heat, Carcassonne and 7 Wonders to US tables.

item.title: KICKSTARTER ALERT! Doomensions Returns slams its pop-up doors at $537,879 — 2,480 backers seal Mysterious Package Company's Crimson Castle & Cursed Tomb for good!
item.description: The Mysterious Package Company's Doomensions Returns closes funded with 2,480 backers, sending its Crimson Castle and Cursed Tomb pop-up escape rooms into production.

item.title: BuzzFeed haunts your autumn to-do list — Doomensions: Mystery Manor pops up beside Murdle and a 100-mystery Agatha Christie puzzle book!
item.description: BuzzFeed's fall roundup slips Mysterious Package Company's pop-up Doomensions: Mystery Manor, Murdle Volume 1 and an Agatha Christie puzzle book among its picks.
